tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Artificial Things — Lucy Bennett

questions.question: Q: What is the choreographic intention of 'Artificial Things'?
questions.correctAnswer: To explore human connection and the idea of finding joy and possibility despite limitations, celebrating how collaboration creates something greater than individual constraints.

questions.question: Q: Why is Stopgap Dance Company significant in the context of this work?
questions.correctAnswer: Stopgap is an integrated company of disabled and non-disabled dancers — the work's meaning depends on this inclusive casting, as the dancers' different bodies directly embody the theme of overcoming limitations.

questions.question: Q: How does David Toole contribute to the work?
questions.correctAnswer: David Toole is a disabled dancer whose powerful upper-body movement, floor work and expressive quality are central to the work — his performance embodies the theme of transcending physical limitations.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Artificial Things — Lucy Bennett

questions.question: Q: Describe the episodic structure of 'Artificial Things'.
questions.correctAnswer: The work is divided into distinct scenes, each exploring a different aspect of human connection — the episodes contrast in mood, movement and design while building the overall theme.

questions.question: Q: How does the costume support the choreographic intention?
questions.correctAnswer: The colourful, casual costumes reflect individual personality and create a warm, human atmosphere — they show the dancers as real people rather than theatrical characters, supporting the theme of authentic human connection.
